object_types.name: Customer
object_types.definition: A person or organization that places orders; identified by a unique customer ID in the CRM system.

source_references.excerpt: A customer places an order.
Each customer has a unique customer ID in the CRM system.
In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients."

object_types.name: Quantity

source_references.excerpt: The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered.

ambiguities.description: The billing team's concept of 'client' requires the person to have actually paid, which is a different definition/state than a CRM 'customer'. Should 'Client' be modeled as a distinct subtype or state of Customer (e.g., a Customer who has made a payment), rather than a pure alias? This affects whether billing-side rules apply to all customers or only a subset.

source_references.excerpt: In our CRM they're "customers" but the billing team calls them "clients." For our purposes they're the same concept but the billing team has a slightly different definition -- they only consider someone a client once they've actually paid.

ambiguities.description: It's unclear whether the order status is a current-state-only attribute or whether history of status changes (e.g., timestamps for pending->confirmed->shipped->delivered) needs to be tracked. This affects whether OrderStatus should be modeled as a simple attribute or as a time-stamped history fact type.

source_references.excerpt: Yes, an order has a status. The possible values are: pending, confirmed, shipped, and delivered.

ambiguities.description: The quantity per order-product line is described as an attribute of the order line, but it's unclear if an order can have multiple lines with the same product (e.g., added at different times) or if product+order is always unique per order. This affects whether the ternary fact type needs an additional 'line number' discriminator.

source_references.excerpt: Each line in the order specifies a product and a quantity.
